summary:
Aladin Lite, a sky viewer running full-window with a saved Orion B observing session. I saved 5 views, and each one replayed with similarity 1.00:
1. sky-view: the main sky view of the Orion belt area with catalogue markers, instrument footprints, the MOC coverage area, the left toolbar, the frame selector, the coordinate box and zoom controls.
2. layer-stack: the layers (Stack) panel listing overlays (notes, YSO candidates, Gaia, SIMBAD, footprints, MOC) and survey layers, each with show/hide, settings and delete buttons.
3. source-measurements: clicking a YSO candidate highlights it and opens the catalogue table at the bottom (class, photometry, status, comment). It shows one row.
4. hips-browser: the floating HiPS browser dialog with wavelength folders, a search field and a filter, opened from Stack > Surveys + > Browse HiPS.
5. note-popup: the callout that opens when you click a "My notes" marker on the sky.

Several views use x/y click positions, because the toolbar buttons and sky markers have no accessible names.

I looked at but did not save these, because they are small dropdowns or popovers: the general settings menu (its tooltip covers part of it), the share menu, the survey settings popover (opacity/colormap) and the catalogue style popover. I could not open the right-click menu because the tool has no right-click action. I also could not get the catalogue table to show more than one row, since clicking the catalogue name in the stack did nothing.

The first save attempts for layer-stack failed twice with "no space left on device" on the harness machine. The third attempt saved, but its recorded steps now include an extra 5-second wait.
